name: Rance tidal electricity generation
description: A tidal station used the rise and fall of water in the Rance estuary to generate electricity.

places.note: Place is a modern geographic reference to the cited episode; it does not imply exclusive origin.

date.basis: Date stated by the cited source.

events.statement: The Rance tidal electricity station in France was inaugurated.
events.caveats: Inauguration does not establish that all of the station’s eventual generators were operating on that day.

evidence.supports: The Rance tidal electricity station in France was inaugurated.
EDF identifies the station and its operation.

date.label: April 2026
date.basis: EDF guide itself bears April 2026; November 9 was only the access date.

events.statement: An EDF guide dated April 2026 reports 240 MW of installed capacity at the Rance tidal station.
events.caveats: This later reported capacity is not assigned to the station’s 1966 inauguration.

evidence.supports: An EDF guide inspected in 2026 reports 240 MW of installed capacity at the Rance tidal station.

earliest_record.rationale: The first sourced event for this particular record, not a claim of a worldwide first.

caveats: The station is one tidal-power system, not evidence of global absence of earlier tidal mills.

measures.subject: Rance station
measures.conditions: EDF guide dated April 2026; not energy output or verified opening-day capacity.

evidence.supports: EDF reports installed capacity of 240 MW.

research.note: Initial sourced admission; interpretation awaits independent review. Independent review checked event source passages and, where marked, measures and relationship scope; other facets retain prior status.
